## The eight AsPredicted questions {#the-eight-aspredicted-questions .smaller}

::: {.fs-80}
| AsPredicted asks | Your block answers |
|---|---|
| Q1 Have data been collected? | "It's complicated – I already hold them", and what I already know, such as the reference estimate of `r fmt_num(curve_ref$b, 3)` |
| Q2 Main question / hypothesis? | the claim, in your own sentence |
| Q3 Dependent variable? | your **outcome**: the couple marry each other in the month |
| Q4 Conditions? | none in the experimental sense: nobody assigned the period in which a union began, and your **surveys** and **cohorts** say which unions are compared |
| Q5 Analyses? | your **adjustment**, **unit**, **time since the start**, **model**, **standard errors** and **scale**, and your rule for support |
| Q6 Outliers / exclusions? | your **women and unions**, **very short unions**, **time frame** and **union histories** |
| Q7 Sample size? | the person-months that your choices leave in: `r fmt_n(min(curve$n))` to `r fmt_n(max(curve$n))` on the curve, of `r fmt_n(min(curve$n_unions))` or `r fmt_n(max(curve$n_unions))` unions |
| Q8 Anything else? | your **weights** and your **education** coding, and your justification, grounded in the causal graph |
:::

::: notes
Each AsPredicted question maps onto a decision that you have already met. The claim, in your own sentence, is question two. Your outcome is the dependent variable. Question four asks about conditions, and here the answer is that there are none, because nobody assigned the period in which a union began; the block records which surveys and cohorts you compare instead. Your adjustment set, the unit, the time term, the model, the standard errors and the scale are the analysis, together with the rule, written before you run anything, for what would count as support. Which women and unions, the short unions, the time frame and the union histories are your exclusions, and they set the sample size. And question one you answer directly: the data exist, I hold them, and here is what I already know.
:::
